claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization and coercivity below approximately 100 Oe.
An intermediate-temperature anneal at 600–700 °C under an inert atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
The proposed anneal will nucleate nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates in FeCoNi.
The annealing-induced precipitates will be uniformly dispersed and coherent with the fcc matrix.
The secondary phase may be B2 or BCC while the surrounding matrix remains fcc.
Secondary-phase precipitates act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
Coherent precipitate interfaces impede domain-wall propagation.
Impeded domain-wall propagation raises the energy barrier for magnetization reversal and thereby increases coercivity.
Annealing-induced phase decomposition and fine BCC precipitation can accompany an increase in coercivity.
Uniform nanoscale precipitation will preserve the high saturation magnetization of the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
The annealed alloy will have coercivity above 100 Oe and may reach several hundred Oe.
The saturation magnetization of the annealed alloy will remain largely comparable to that of the as-cast single-phase alloy.
The expected effect applies to near-equiatomic FeCoNi compositions processed under controlled inert atmospheres.
Excessive secondary-phase growth may reduce magnetization or cause unwanted brittleness.
The magnitude of coercivity enhancement and the optimum precipitate distribution depend on annealing temperature, duration, and cooling rate.
TEM and XRD can test whether the anneal produced the intended secondary phase, while magnetic hysteresis measurements can determine coercivity and saturation magnetization.

The hypothesis is falsified if precipitate-bearing annealed samples remain below or statistically equivalent to 100 Oe, or if increased coercivity requires a substantial loss of saturation magnetization.
